prior_importants.description: PROTECTED_WITHIN_EXCEPTIONS keeps only `.claude/skills/pr-ci-review/**` protected, but the CI review allows a bare `"Skill"` permission, so any other worker-merged skill can be loaded by every later CI review with the repo token — the harm ADR 0208 gives as its reason for protecting pr-ci-review.

The gate protects the CI review's skill by directory, but skills resolve by frontmatter `name:`: a new `.claude/skills/<x>/SKILL.md` declaring `name: pr-ci-review` passes the gate and competes for the `/pr-ci-review` command the workflow runs with the repo token. The ADR's premise that a skill is inert prose is also wrong, since frontmatter like `allowed-tools` is acted on.

findings.description: The non-regular-file refusal only runs for a path `isSkillManifest` matches, but `.claude/skills/**/*.md` also lifts `.claude/skills/shadow.md`. Committed as a symlink to a directory (e.g. `../../docs/shadow`, holding a `SKILL.md` with `name: pr-ci-review`), that path is never read and its mode is never checked, so the scope audit passes it.

The new name check fails open because `FRONTMATTER`/`FRONTMATTER_OPENING` are narrower than Claude Code's frontmatter parser at both delimiters. (A) An opening `---` followed by NBSP, `\f` or `\v` before the LF matches neither regex, so `isMisnamedSkill` returns false. (B) A `---` in the middle of a line, as in `name: pr-ci-review---`, does not close the block for the gate, but a lazy reader closes there.
findings.body:
**The `SKILL.md` name check can be bypassed through frontmatter delimiter mismatches**

`isMisnamedSkill` is safe only if it reads at least the frontmatter Claude Code reads; the comment says it reads "wider than Claude Code may". At both delimiters it reads narrower:

```ts
const FRONTMATTER = /^﻿?\s*---[ \t]*\r?\n((?:[\s\S]*?\r?\n)?)---[ \t]*(?:\r?\n|$)/;
const FRONTMATTER_OPENING = /^﻿?\s*---[ \t]*\r?\n/;
...
if (block === null) return FRONTMATTER_OPENING.test(content);
```

1. **Opening line.** The gate accepts only a space, tab or CR between `---` and the LF. Take `.claude/skills/zz/SKILL.md` = `"--- \nname: pr-ci-review\n---\n"` (or `\f`, `\v` or another Unicode space after `---`). It matches neither regex, so `isMisnamedSkill` returns `false` and the scope audit passes it. A parser that opens on `^---\s*\n`, where JS `\s` includes NBSP, reads a skill named `pr-ci-review`.
2. **Closing delimiter.** The gate closes only on a line that starts with `---`. Take `.claude/skills/pr-ci-review---/SKILL.md` = `"---\nname: pr-ci-review---\n---\n"`. It is not under `.claude/skills/pr-ci-review/**`, and the gate's name equals the directory, so it passes. A lazy `([\s\S]*?)---` closes inside the value and reads `name: pr-ci-review`.

Both lead to the outcome the check exists to stop: a skill outside the protected directory that answers `/pr-ci-review`. Claude Code's exact parser isn't in-tree, hence medium confidence. The existing test `'a line a looser reader closes on'` covers only a `---` at the start of a line.

**Fix:** fail closed in both places. Refuse any manifest that starts (after an optional BOM and whitespace) with `---` but doesn't match the strict block, which makes `FRONTMATTER_OPENING` obsolete. Refuse any block whose YAML contains `---`. Add both inputs above to `skill-name-utils.test.ts`.

<https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/77c0dfe4ff4f3bcc6a48d74abbd91e8262957f48/src/core/skill-name.utils.ts#L12-L35>

findings.description: The gate closes frontmatter only at a `---` that starts a line, so `.claude/skills/pr-ci-review---/SKILL.md` with `name: pr-ci-review---` passes: its name equals its directory. A reader that closes at the first `---` anywhere reads `name: pr-ci-review` and registers `/pr-ci-review`.
findings.body:
**A mid-line `---` lets a skill outside the protected directory answer `/pr-ci-review`**

`FRONTMATTER` only closes at a `---` that starts a line:

```ts
const FRONTMATTER = /^﻿?\s*---[ \t]*\r?\n((?:[\s\S]*?\r?\n)?)---[ \t]*(?:\r?\n|$)/;
```

Take a branch that adds `.claude/skills/pr-ci-review---/SKILL.md`:

```
---
name: pr-ci-review---
---
```

The gate does this with it:

- The path does not match `.claude/skills/pr-ci-review/**`, which needs a `/` right after the name.
- The path is lifted by `.claude/skills/**/*.md`.
- The gate parses `name: pr-ci-review---`. That equals the directory, and lowercased it is not `pr-ci-review`, so `isMisnamedSkill` returns `false` and the file merges.

A reader that closes at the first `---` anywhere, as a lazy `^---\s*\n([\s\S]*?)---` does, reads `name: pr-ci-review` and registers the slash command the CI workflow runs. That is the shadowing this delta sets out to stop. Claude Code's parser isn't in-tree, hence medium confidence. The test `'a line a looser reader closes on'` covers only a `---` at the start of a line.

**Fix:** fail closed when the YAML block contains `---` anywhere. Any reader that closes earlier then reads a shorter block than the gate did, and the file is refused.

<https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/77c0dfe4ff4f3bcc6a48d74abbd91e8262957f48/src/core/skill-name.utils.ts#L34-L35>

findings.description: The rescope still accepts any wildcard glob whose fixed prefix lies under `.claude/skills/`, even after the exception was narrowed to `.claude/skills/**/*.md`. `within` only compares prefixes. So `.claude/skills/wizard/*.sh` or `.claude/skills/**/scripts/*` is taken, though every path it can match is refused by the gate as a protected path, and the literal `.claude/skills/wizard/template.sh` is refused by the rescope. The worker is granted scope it can never merge, which surfaces only as a full gate run ending in rejection. The `reachesProtected` JSDoc ("also reaches a skill's scripts") doesn't describe globs that reach nothing else.

`branchBlobReader` spells the shape `{ mode: string; oid: string }[]` out three times: on `sides`, on the `readSides` return type, and on `read`. Changing the record shape means editing all three. A single local type, or dropping the `readSides` return annotation and letting it infer, removes the repetition.
